messages:
Sasha: Heads up — noticed our onboarding sampleapp (js + go-sdk combo) burned through quota yesterday when PREFETCH was enabled. Repro below, seems tied to paginator + client-side throttling/backpressure.
Tyler: How bad was it? any numbers or traces? 😬
Sasha: Metrics show ~8x expected token usage for a short window. Lots of 429s followed by retries which amplified the token burn.
Andrew: Can you paste the paginator config / logs?
Sasha: Config snippet from sampleapp: 
```js
const paginator = new Paginator({
  prefetch: true,
  concurrency: 4,
  pageSize: 50,
})
```
And from the Go worker we saw goroutine loop like: 
```go
for token := range pageTokens {
  go func(t string) {
    // fetch page, no singleflight, no inflight dedupe
    fetchPage(ctx, t)
  }(token)
}
```
Log excerpt: 
```
WARN token-limiter: throttle delay=200ms
INFO pager: fetching page=3 attempt=1
INFO pager: fetching page=3 attempt=2
INFO pager: fetching page=3 attempt=3
```
Maria: That pattern explains it — prefetch spawns parallel fetches and the rate limiter delays responses, so retries pile up. Without an inflight dedupe or proper cancellation you get duplicate downstream requests.
Tyler: Is this specific to Go SDK? JS behaves differently?
Sasha: JS had a small mutex around in-flight prefetches and serializes a page key; Go tried to be optimistic and spawned per-token goroutines.
devex-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-145 — sampleapp prefetch duplicate fetches causing quota surge
Lucy: Quick mitigation: add an inflight map keyed by page token + use singleflight.Group to dedupe. Also make prefetch call limiter.Acquire(ctx) before spawning or cancel goroutine when limiter blocks too long.
Andrew: Test plan idea: run a local token-bucket limiter to force backpressure: `TOKEN_BUCKET capacity=10 refill=2/s` then run sampleapp with CONCURRENCY=8 and PREFETCH=true to reproduce.
Sasha: I ran that locally, reproduces reliably in ~30s. Repro steps: start dedicated with low qps; set env PREFETCH=true; set CONCURRENCY=8; run load script (see gist) and watch 429 -> retries -> token spike.
Tyler: Any API surface changes needed? we should avoid breaking user behavior.
Maria: No public API changes needed — internal concurrency/dedupe fix only. Should be transparent.
Sasha: I'll open a PR with the following: singleflight dedupe, prefetch respects limiter.Acquire(ctx) with low timeout, unit test simulating 429 and stress harness. Assigning Andrew for review and Maria for parity check with JS.
Andrew: Ack — will prioritize review today. Also propose an e2e that asserts "no duplicate upstream requests" metric under induced 429s.
Lucy: :thumbsup: Add telemetry counter for dedupe hits and a test that asserts it increases under contention.
Sasha: Thanks — aiming for a patch by EOD and will post PR link here when ready.
